newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-PRESSURE ON GERMANY AHEAD OF UKRAINE MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PRESSURE ON GERMANY AHEAD OF UKRAINE MATCH.

text.p: Germany will have their backs to the wall in the race for a spot in the World Cup finals when their injury-depleted team plays host to front-running Ukraine on Wednesday.

Stuck in third place in qualifying group nine behind Ukraine and Portugal, Germany desperately need a victory in Bremen to keep alive their hopes of winning the group and guaranteed themselves a place in the World Cup finals next year.
"It is the most important match of the year," said coach Berti Vogts, whose Euro 96-winning team has struggled with two draws and two wins in the group so far.
Ukraine have won four of their five matches and lead the group with 12 points. Portugal are second with nine points.

"We need three points if we want to fight our way directly to the World Cup finals in France," Vogts said. "I am convinced the team will put in a stronger performance than in recent games. The harder the opponents, the easier it will be for us."
Germany have certainly made it look difficult against easier opponents.
The 1990 World Cup winners managed draws against Northern Ireland and Portugal and have beaten only lowly Armenia and Albania.
The Albanians nearly defeated Germany in their most recent qualifier before Ulf Kirsten came off the bench to score a hat-trick in a 3-2 win.
But Kirsten is suspended for the match against Ukraine.
"The team knows what is at stake -- we need two wins, no matter how," said Bayern Munich's Mario Basler, who is expected to replaced the injured Andy Moeller in midfield.
Vogts will be missing many other key players due to injury. Matthias Sammer, Stefan Reuter and Lars Ricken as well as Moeller have all been declared unfit for the match in Bremen's Weser Stadium.

"Every player is replaceable," said Vogts, who also dismissed criticism from Borussia Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld that internationals were becoming so vulnerable to injury because they were playing so many matches.
"I can't understand all the moaning and complaining," Vogts said. "These are professionals and they earn a lot of money. It is up to them to work on their own health and fitness in training."

One injured player Vogts will most likely be able to rely on is goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, who has been suffering from a hamstring injury. Koepke dropped out of a training session in Bremen on Monday but said it was just a preventative measure.
"I just didn't want to overtax the muscle," Koepke said.

Vogts has enlisted three newcomers to the squad -- Jens Jeremies from 1860 Munich, Sven Kmetsch from Hamburg and Jens Nowotny from Bayer Leverkusen. None is expected to start the match against Ukraine.
Germany - Andreas Koepke, Thomas Helmer, Markus Babbel, Juergen Kohler, Joerg Heinrich, Dieter Eilts, Christian Ziege, Mario Basler, Dariusz Wosz, Juergen Klinsmann, Oliver Bierhoff
Ukraine - Oleg Suslov, Oleksandr Golovko, Oleg Luzhnyi, Vladislav Vashchyuk, Viktor Skripnik, Sergiy Bezhenar, Yuri Maksimov, Gennady Orbu, Yuri Kalitvintsev, Vitaly Kosovsky, Andriy Shevchenko
